ARKFLAME STUDIOS · PRIVACY

Privacy policy.

A clear explanation of what Global DOM Optimizer does with the webpage information it encounters.

Global DOM Optimizer v0.0.6Effective October 11, 2026Publisher: ArkFlame Studios

ON THIS PAGE

Purpose & processing Local storage Collection & sharing Permissions Your controls Limited Use Contact & updates
✓

Rendering stays on your device.

Global DOM Optimizer reads page structure only to optimize rendering, and it does that inside your browser. The extension has no telemetry or analytics endpoint and doesn't upload page content to ArkFlame Studios.

1. Purpose and local processing

Global DOM Optimizer makes rendering more efficient on eligible pages. Its content script checks document structure, text lengths, element sizes, scroll containers, and viewport or scroll positions. It finds elements that can safely use native CSS offscreen rendering containment, and restores rendering as content nears the visible area.

This runs inside the browser. The extension doesn't upload or copy page text, images, personal messages or other page content to ArkFlame Studios.

2. Information stored locally

The extension uses chrome.storage.local for the global on/off setting and the hostnames the user excludes. These settings stay on the device. The extension doesn't sync them.

The popup shows current-tab diagnostics: managed or hidden block counts, scroll-region info and scan timings. These values pass through browser-internal messaging. They aren't uploaded to the publisher or saved as a browsing history.

3. Collection, sharing and retention

ArkFlame Studios doesn't receive page contents, personal communications, browsing history, scrolling activity, authentication information or diagnostic metrics from the extension. Version 0.0.6 has no tracking, analytics, ad SDK, external API calls or remotely executed code. It doesn't sell or share extension user data with third parties.

Local settings stay until you change them, clear extension data in your browser, or uninstall the extension. Browser storage rules apply.

4. Permissions and website access

The extension runs local content scripts on HTTP and HTTPS pages to inspect eligible elements and apply rendering styles. It needs this cross-site access because its main job is automatic optimization across pages.

  • storage: saves the global switch and the sites you exclude, locally.
  • activeTab: lets the popup, which you open, read the current site's hostname and local diagnostics.
  • HTTP/HTTPS content scripts: identify eligible offscreen DOM sections and adjust their rendering containment.

The extension doesn't request cookies, browser history, network interception or downloads permissions. Chrome blocks content scripts on some internal or restricted pages.

5. Your controls

Use the popup to turn optimization off everywhere or for the current site. Either choice reverses the styles the extension manages. Some elements and whole sites may stay unchanged when safe containment isn't possible.

6. Limited Use and security

Global DOM Optimizer uses the information it accesses only for its offscreen-rendering feature and related on-device diagnostics. Its use of information received from Google APIs follows the Chrome Web Store User Data Policy, including its Limited Use requirements. The extension doesn't run remotely hosted scripts.

7. External publisher link

The popup has an optional link to ArkFlame Studios. Clicking it opens the publisher's website. The extension doesn't send page content or diagnostic data with that navigation. Site access is separate from the extension's local processing.

8. Updates and contact

Material changes to the extension's data practices will appear in this policy and in the Chrome Web Store disclosures before they are published. For questions, contact ArkFlame Studios through arkflame.com.

This policy describes Global DOM Optimizer version 0.0.6. Other ArkFlame Studios services may operate under separate notices.
